'''Aleksandar Popović''' ({{lang-sr-Cyrl|Александар Поповић}}, {{IPA|sr|aleksǎːndar pǒpoʋit͜ɕ|pron}} <small>or</small> {{IPA|sr|alěksaːndar|}}, born 20 October 1971) is a Serbian politician and university professor. He served as the [[Ministry of Mining and Energy (Serbia)|Minister of Energy and Mining]] from 2007 to 2008, and as the [[Ministry of Science (Serbia)|Minister of Science and Environmental Protection]] from 2004 to 2007.<ref>http://www.arhiva.serbia.gov.rs/cms/view.php?id=1192#popovic Ministers of the Serbian Government</ref> Before becoming a politician, Popović was a sprinter who competed internationally throughout 1990s.

==Education==
Internationally educated, Popović completed elementary school in [[Belgrade]] before moving to [[Moscow]] where he finished high school. Returning home to complete college, he obtained a degree from [[University of Belgrade]]'s Faculty of Chemistry. During the mid-1990s he moved abroad again, this time to [[Tallahassee]], in [[Florida]], [[United States]], where in 1996 he earned his [[Master's degree|MA]] from [[Florida State University]]. Finally in 2002, he added a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] to his academic resume from Faculty of Chemistry in Belgrade, where he currently works as a full [[professor]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.chem.bg.ac.rs/osoblje/47-en.html |title=Aleksandar R. Popović, Ph.D. |website=chem.bg.ac.rs |publisher=[[University of Belgrade]] |access-date=July 26, 2021}}</ref>

==Athletic career==
Popović made his international debut at the [[1990 World Junior Championships in Athletics]], where he ran in Heat 6 of the [[1990 World Junior Championships in Athletics – Men's 100 metres|men's 100 meters]] as well as in Heat 5 of the [[1990 World Junior Championships in Athletics – Men's 200 metres|men's 200 meters]]. In neither distance did he make it into the semifinals. When he moved to Moscow, he continued training with [[Dynamo Sports Club]].<ref name="Glas">{{cite web|url=http://arhiva.glas-javnosti.rs/arhiva/2006/08/06/srpski/R06080501.shtml|author=Aleksandra Klarić-Žak|title=Glas Javnosti: ''U politiku utrčao sa atletske staze''|language=Serbian|date=August 6, 2006|accessdate=December 26, 2016}}</ref> When he studied for his master's degree at Florida State, he trained with the varsity team but was not [[NCAA]] eligible, so he ran unattached at college track meets.<ref name="Glas"/> Upon returning to Yugoslavia from his graduate studies in the United States, he was called up as a member of Yugoslavia's [[4 × 400 metres relay]] team for the [[Athletics at the 1997 Mediterranean Games – Results|1997 Mediterranean Games]], which placed last at the competition.<ref name="Glas"/> His competitive sprinting career ended in 1999 with a [[Tear of meniscus|meniscus injury]].<ref name="Glas"/> His personal record in the 200 meters was 21.73 seconds with no wind aid.<ref name="All-Athletics">{{cite web|url=http://www.all-athletics.com/node/71827|title=Profile of Aleksander POPOVIĆ (born 20.10.1971)|accessdate=December 26, 2016}}</ref>

==Political career==
Popović was the Vice-president of [[Democratic Party of Serbia]] between 2003 and 2016.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://dss.rs/dss-izbliza/organi-stranke/potpredsednici/ |title=ПОТПРЕДСЕДНИЦИ &#124; Демократска странка Србије |accessdate=2012-03-17 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120314005747/http://dss.rs/dss-izbliza/organi-stranke/potpredsednici/ |archivedate=2012-03-14 }} Democratic Party of Serbia Vice-Presidents (in Serbian)</ref>
He served as the Minister of Energy and Mining and previously Minister of Science and Environmental Protection in both [[Vojislav Koštunica|Koštunica]]'s Governments between 2004 and 2008.
He was [[Democratic Party of Serbia|DSS]] candidate for the [[Belgrade]] City Mayor position in both [[2008 Serbian local elections]]<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.b92.co.rs/eng/news/comments.php?nav_id=48683 |title=B92 - News - Comments - DSS-NS submit Belgrade list |accessdate=2012-03-17 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://archive.today/20120724091309/http://www.b92.co.rs/eng/news/comments.php?nav_id=48683 |archivedate=2012-07-24 }} DSS-NS submit Belgrade list, March 21, 2008. Retrieved: March 17, 2012</ref> and [[2012 Serbian local elections]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.tanjug.rs/news/35549/belgrade-to-get-66th-mayor.htm |title=Belgrade to get 66th mayor &#124; Vesti &#124; Tanjug |accessdate=2012-03-17 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://archive.today/20120912043446/http://www.tanjug.rs/news/35549/belgrade-to-get-66th-mayor.htm |archivedate=2012-09-12 }} Belgrade to get 66th Mayor, March 14, 2012. Retrieved: March 17, 2012</ref> He was nominated as [[Democratic Party of Serbia]]'s candidate in the [[2017 Serbian presidential election]].

==Political positions==
===Economic policy===
During a 2017 presidential campaign stop in [[Niš]], Popović called for reducing the [[Value-added tax|value-added tax rates]] on all domestic production in underdeveloped parts of Serbia.<ref name="RadioNis">{{cite web|url=http://www.radiocity.rs/izbori-2017/6558/popovic-%E2%80%9Enizi-pdv-za-proizvodnju-u-nerazvijenim-delovima-zemlje%E2%80%9C.html|author=Aleksandar Đokić|title=99.9 FM City RADIO :''Popović: "Niži PDV za proizvodnju u nerazvijenim delovima zemlje"''|language=Serbian|date=March 21, 2017|accessdate=March 24, 2017}}</ref> He also called for a [[progressive tax]] regarding those with higher incomes, however unlike the typical progressive tax model, Popović told his campaign audience in [[Sremska Mitrovica]] that the poorest should not pay taxes at all.<ref name="SrbijadanasPopovic">{{cite web|url=https://www.srbijadanas.com/vesti/izbori-2017/popovic-vreme-je-da-bogati-placaju-vece-poreze-najsiromasniji-da-ga-ne-placaju-uopste-2017-03-16|author=Srbija Danas|title=''POPOVIĆ: Ovi izbori su važni jer predstavljaju vraćanje slobode''|language=Serbian|date=March 16, 2017|accessdate=March 24, 2017}}</ref>

Without mentioning his name, Popović said that Minister of Finance [[Dušan Vujović]] is "an excellent professional", but criticized him on the deadlines given to Serbian [[Member of parliament|MPs]] on assessing budget proposals.<ref name="Blic28">{{cite web|url=http://www.blic.rs/vesti/politika/popovic-najverovatnije-cu-biti-predsednicki-kandidat-dss-a/9czegl8|title=Blic: ''Popović: Najverovatnije ću biti predsednički kandidat DSS-a''|date=February 8, 2017|accessdate=February 19, 2017}}</ref> Popović claimed that such deadlines were meant to satisfy the conveniences of the [[International Monetary Fund|IMF]] as opposed to the interests of Serbia.<ref name="Blic28"/>

===Foreign policy===
====European Union====
Popović is a long-time [[euroscepticism|eurosceptic]]. In an interview with ''[[Večernje novosti]]'' on January 24, 2017, Popović stated that he was against the [[Brussels Agreement (2013)|Brussels Agreement]].<ref name="NovostiBrisel">{{cite web|url=http://www.novosti.rs/vesti/naslovna/politika/aktuelno.289.html:646182-Aleksandar-Popovic-Ukinuo-bih-briselske-sporazume|author=D. R. ĐORĐEVIĆ|title=Novosti: ''Aleksandar Popović: Ukinuo bih briselske sporazume''|date=January 24, 2017|accessdate=February 19, 2017}}</ref> He suggested that even the termination of the Brussels Agreement should not mean an end to diplomatic relations with the [[European Union]], but that Serbia in that case should still abstain from EU membership.<ref name="MondoDSS">{{cite web|url=http://mondo.rs/a993115/Info/Srbija/Predsednicki-izbori-Popovic-o-saradnji-sa-EU.html|author=Mondo|title=''Popović: Saradnja s Briselom, ali ne SSP''|language=Serbian|date=March 22, 2017|accessdate=March 24, 2017}}</ref> During a visit in [[Smederevo]] during his presidential campaign, Popović told the press that the European Union would try to prevent Chinese investments into the Serbian metallurgical industry.<ref name="Blic28"/>
